limitations: One fresh run per mode is a bounded repair confirmation against existing unchanged frozen limits; not a new five-run baseline or population tail estimate.
Native reports NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090/Vulkan/610.43.03; Chromium 151.0.7922.34 reports NVIDIA/Ampere and withholds device model. Other GPU/browser/network environments remain unqualified.

Fresh service and native client start with no application cache; first observation is uncontrolled-first-observation. Browser/recovery follow completed service journeys and use warm-server. OS/page/NFS source-storage cache state is uncontrolled; reuse is file identity, not a physical-storage-coldness claim.

First useful means first primary-region residency. Whole overview separately includes 121 primary regions and visible gallery. GPU resource bytes describe logical textures, not physical allocation overhead or device completion/scanout.

Browser process memory is 50 ms sampled Linux descendant RSS excluding Node; shared mappings may count repeatedly. Observed per-PID VmHWM sums combine nonsimultaneous peaks and can miss short-lived unsampled processes.

Recovery cumulative work sums sampled maxima per context, resource peaks remain maxima; three total workers are sequential fresh contexts, not concurrency. Recovery restores transport, not the service process.

128-event/64-checksum rings and snapshots are bounded. Large intermediate histories are hash-indexed in this package and remain in registered scratch until coordinator cleanup; compact stage summaries omit events/checksum arrays that are separately retained where stated.
No protected or real imagery was used. Public repair qualification does not establish representative real-image preparation or complete satellite-image objective qualification.
